claims.text: Equiatomic CrCoNi is a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy.
The strength–ductility synergy of FCC CrCoNi under dynamic loading is primarily controlled by deformation-induced nanoscale twinning.
Nanoscale twin networks form and evolve during deformation of CrCoNi.
Dynamically formed stacking-fault networks contribute to the mechanical behavior of the proposed single-phase FCC CrCoNi system.
Mechanical loading locally lowers the effective stacking-fault energy.
Low stacking-fault energy promotes twinning in FCC CrCoNi.
Twin boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength and strain hardening.
Twin boundaries provide additional slip systems or glide channels that enhance ductility and delay failure.
Deformation nanotwinning becomes more prominent at cryogenic temperatures.
An as-processed, quenched CrCoNi sample will have minimal pre-existing twin networks.
A defect-reducing thermomechanical processing route can suppress dynamic twin formation while preserving a suitable comparison state.
Relative to a non-twinning or twinning-suppressed baseline, a dynamically twinning sample will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the baseline, a dynamically twinning sample will have a delayed onset of necking and greater uniform elongation.
Work-hardening rate will increase in correlation with twin density and twin-network evolution.
The proposed mechanism should apply broadly to low-to-moderate-stacking-fault-energy FCC high-entropy alloys under conditions that activate twinning.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to high-stacking-fault-energy alloys or to BCC or HCP high-entropy alloys.
Stress-induced phase transformation can compete with twinning-related mechanisms in some high-entropy alloys.
The quantitative strengthening contribution and plasticity mechanism associated with deformation twinning in CrCoNi remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The conditions field permits a quasi-static baseline, whereas the baseline and falsification experiment call for comparable or identical strain-rate conditions. A quasi-static comparison would change the loading regime and would not isolate twinning suppression as the controlled variable.
